correctness.rationale: Equality and the two directed strict-ancestry comparisons with each mark determine a type. The nonempty descendant-mark supports are laminar, giving at most 2m−1; equal nonempty supports put their vertices on one path to a shared mark, and no mark between the vertices can change their ancestor profile without changing the support. With empty support the deepest marked ancestor, or its absence, selects at most m+1 further signatures. The equality case saturates both counts: the support family contains all singletons and the whole set and its inclusion tree is full binary. Singleton supports force pairwise incomparable marks, so the remaining types require exactly an unmarked strict descendant for each mark and an unmarked vertex incomparable with all marks. Attaching mark-terminal pairs at the hierarchy leaves and one extra offshoot realizes all profiles in 4m vertices of outdegree at most two, including m=1; fewer vertices cannot realize 4m types. On a path the m+1 gaps and m marks are attained by alternation. Conjunctions isolate individual type classes, and arbitrary unions give exactly 2^t definable sets.
correctness.verification_limits: The proof is unbounded. The frozen checks/verify_tree_types.py was inspected, not executed: its tree enumeration covers orders 2–6 and its constructions m=1–12; those checks are corroboration only.
